data_policy: All values are verbatim from the source workbook. No synthetic or demo data.

modules.title: CALL LIST - TOP 100
modules.subtitle: START HERE — the 100 highest-opportunity real customers, ranked. Work top-down. "pitch_angle" is what to say; "likely_reason_gap_or_churn" is what probably went wrong. ROWS SHADED PINK HAVE NO PHONE NUMBER on file — trace the contact before you get to them.

modules.title: LAPSED BIG ACCOUNTS
modules.subtitle: THE MPS LIMITED PROBLEM — every real customer who billed Rs 1 lakh or more and has not ordered in 120+ days. They already trust Oakcraft and already paid once. A senior person should make these calls, not a junior telecaller. Pink rows have no phone on file.

modules.title: DEALER & CHANNEL TARGETS
modules.subtitle: 54 businesses researched as being IN THE FURNITURE OR SEATING TRADE — dealers, retailers, wholesalers and furniture manufacturers. Several file GST under the same HSN codes as Oakcraft (9401/9403). They are buying from you at retail when they should be on dealer terms. Converting even ten of these into stocking partners changes the revenue base permanently. Read the "what_they_do" column before you call — it says exactly what each one sells.

modules.title: ARCHITECTS & INTERIORS
modules.subtitle: SPEC-IN ACCOUNTS — interior designers, architects, turnkey fitout firms, joinery and furniture manufacturers. These do not buy once; they specify furniture into every project they win. One good relationship here is worth more than fifty retail orders. Ask what is in their pipeline, not what they need today.

modules.title: OTHER RESELLERS
modules.subtitle: TRADERS IN ADJACENT GOODS — IT hardware, office stationery, medical equipment, building materials, electricals. They are NOT furniture traders, so do not treat them as dealers. But they already sell into offices, clinics and institutions, which means they can carry Oakcraft seating alongside what they stock. Check the "what_they_do" column: it tells you what they actually sell, so you can pitch the right bundle.

modules.title: INSTITUTIONS, GOVT & PSU
modules.subtitle: TENDER-WATCH LIST, built from the RESEARCHED business type (not the original file's labels, which were wrong on many rows). Oakcraft is a Micro MSE and the OEM, so it qualifies for MSE purchase preference (L1+15%) on GeM. WARNING: Oakcraft holds NO BIS certificate — if a bid makes BIS mandatory, skip it before spending any effort.

modules.title: CORPORATES
modules.subtitle: REGISTERED COMPANIES ONLY — every row here is a Pvt Ltd or Ltd company confirmed by its GST entity code AND researched as a corporate. They buy on new floors, new branches and 4-6 year refresh cycles. The goal on these calls is not an order today; it is getting Oakcraft onto their approved-vendor list so the next requirement comes to you automatically.

modules.title: ACTIVE REPEAT - PROTECT
modules.subtitle: YOUR CHAMPIONS — active, repeat, paying. This tab is defensive, not offensive. These accounts carry most of the business; losing one costs more than winning three new ones. Give them first look at new models, and never let a service complaint sit.

modules.title: ONE-TIME BUYERS
modules.subtitle: 396 real customers who ordered ONCE and never came back, sorted by value. The top of this list is where the money is — a Rs 8 lakh single order is a failed relationship, not a retail sale. Below roughly Rs 25,000, do not spend field time: run those as a bulk WhatsApp or email campaign.

modules.title: NEAR FACTORY - VISIT
modules.subtitle: Customers inside or beside your own Bawana / Poothkhurd / Narela / Rithala belt. Freight is near zero and a salesperson can walk in unannounced. Batch these into one or two field days — the cheapest cost-per-meeting in the whole file.

modules.title: NO PHONE ON FILE
modules.subtitle: 105 accounts worth calling that have NO PHONE NUMBER in the master file. Do not let these die silently. Most have a GSTIN and a full address — the number can be traced from the GST portal, IndiaMART, JustDial or the invoice copy. Together these carry real money; get the numbers first, then merge them into tab 02.

modules.title: DUPLICATES & SHARED PHONES
modules.subtitle: READ THE "Group" COLUMN BEFORE YOU MERGE ANYTHING. GROUP 1 is safe to merge - every record carries the same GSTIN, or the names differ only by a Mr/Ms prefix or a spelling slip. GROUP 2 needs a phone call first: the addresses or order values match but the names differ, which is usually a person recorded once by their own name and once by their firm name. GROUPS 3 AND 4 MUST NOT BE MERGED - those are separate legal businesses sharing one address or promoter group, a name coincidence across two states, or records linked only by an Oakcraft staff phone number. Merging a Group 3 or 4 pair destroys a real customer record.

modules.title: DATA TO CLEAN
modules.subtitle: 29 RECORDS THAT ARE NOT REAL CUSTOMERS: internal and staff billing (including rows carrying Oakcraft's OWN GSTIN 07ABOPM2275Q1ZV and rows billed to your own Poothkhurd factory address), Rs 0-2 test orders, customer names stored as addresses or as GSTINs,  Every other tab in this workbook already excludes them. Clean them out of the CRM so your reports and your team's call lists stop counting them.
